description: LLM-powered meeting recap system that produces two complementary views of a meeting transcript: (1) a quick highlights recap (key points + action items) and (2) a hierarchical minutes-style recap segmented into topically-coherent chapters with rolling 3rd-person summaries. Built on top of unsupervised dialogue topic segmentation driven by an utterance-pair NSP-BERT coherence scorer + TextTiling.
data_corpus_note: data/eval_vi/ contains Vietnamese-translated versions of paper-1's English test sets (dialseg_711, doc2dial), paper-2's AMI/ICSI meeting corpora (meeting_ami, meeting_icsi), plus the project's own meeting_committee sample and tiage. ZYS (Chinese) is NOT shipped with this repo -- the eval-001 feature must source it externally if Chinese segmentation is in scope.

known_gaps.gap: Highlight model is missing `assigned_to` and `due_date` fields that paper-2 Section 3.4 specifies as editable per action item. This blocks the exact paper-2 UX in ui-001. A follow-up patch must add these fields (with Pydantic validators) before ui-001's 'edit task assignee/deadline' verification can pass.

NSP-BERT paper-1 model is described as 'fine-tuned' on DailyDialog (en) / NaturalConv (zh). The project does not ship a fine-tuned checkpoint; it must either load a public fine-tuned checkpoint or include a fine-tuning step. For Vietnamese, a separate Vietnamese NSP-BERT must be sourced or trained.

features.notes: Pydantic v2 BaseModels on a shared BaseSchema (extra='forbid', populate_by_name, str_strip_whitespace) for schema safety, JSON serialization, and FastAPI integration. Composable via composition (Transcript -> Segment -> Chunk -> Utterance) so model-002 loader and svc-001/svc-002 services can plug in without re-shaping data. Immutability for Utterance, mutable semantics for Highlight (toggle_star/toggle_check) match the recap paper's interactive UX. Canonical enum names follow the paper (KEY_POINT, ACTION_ITEM); UX labels (note / task, or Vietnamese ghi chú / việc cần làm) are applied at the i18n boundary, not in the enum, so the data layer stays language-neutral. MAX_UTTERANCES is enforced both on the domain object and at the request boundary, so oversized meetings fail fast with a clear message.

Five transformers total: one BART for hierarchical_segment, two deBERTa for hierarchical_abstractive / hierarchical_title, one BART for highlights_extractive, one deBERTa for highlights_abstractive (paper-2 Table 1), plus the NSP-BERT coherence scorer from paper-1. KNOWN GAP: NSP-BERT must be either fine-tuned from BERT_base (paper-1 Section 3.2) on DailyDialog/NaturalConv, or sourced from a public fine-tuned checkpoint. Vietnamese NSP-BERT is not shipped; a separate per-language checkpoint strategy is required (paper-1 Section 4.5 reports smaller gains for Chinese, suggesting per-language fine-tuning is necessary).

features.notes: Derived directly from paper-1 Section 3 and paper-2 Section 3.3. The 8-words-per-utterance heuristic (Banerjee et al.) and the 1 token = 0.75 words heuristic justify the window/stride/chunk sizes. Stride > window is invalid for a sliding-window TextTiling pipeline; reject it loudly. Paper-1 Section 3.3 does not prescribe a fixed smoothing or cutoff -- expose them but mark as 'tune' defaults.

features.title: Implement Utterance-Pair Coherence Scoring (NSP-BERT)
features.user_visible_behavior: Given any two consecutive utterances, the CoherenceScorer returns a depth score (low = same topic, high = topic shift) using the fine-tuned NSP-BERT model from paper-1.
verification: Pass a same-topic utterance pair from data/eval_vi/meeting_committee.json to CoherenceScorer and assert low depth score.
Pass a topic-shift pair (e.g. cross the turn-4 boundary in the paper-1 Table 1 example) and assert high depth score.
Confirm scores run as a single batched forward pass (no Python-level per-pair loop) on GPU and CPU.
Persist the model checkpoint path so the same weights are reused across svc-002 and svc-003 without reloads.
Use DialogueTranscript.utterance_pairs as the canonical input iterator so the scorer never depends on raw indices.
Reuse the NSP tokenizer's [CLS] / [SEP] / segment-embedding contract from paper-1 Section 3.2 verbatim.
features.notes: Paper-1 Section 3.2: train a BERT_base (12 layers, 12 heads, hidden 768) with marginal ranking loss on automatically-constructed positive/negative utterance pairs. The scorer must be a first-class service because both svc-002 (TextTiling) and any future per-chapter coherence checks consume it. Paper-1 Section 3.2 also notes the cross-encoder (NSP) was chosen over bi-encoder because cross-encoders outperform bi-encoders for pairwise scoring (Thakur et al., 2021) -- this justification must be carried in code comments.

features.title: Implement TextTiling Segmentation with Sliding-Window Max-Voting
features.user_visible_behavior: Given a DialogueTranscript, TextTilingService returns an ordered list of segment boundaries (start_index, end_index) using a 30-utterance sliding window, stride of 10, and max-voting over CoherenceScorer predictions (paper-1 Section 3, paper-2 Section 3.2).
verification: Run TextTiling on data/eval_vi/meeting_committee.json[0] and confirm the predicted segment count is in [6, 10] for the 8 ground-truth segments.
Confirm per-window scores, the depth-score sequence, and the max-vote tally are all exposed for debugging.
Reject transcripts longer than DialogueTranscript.MAX_UTTERANCES with a typed error before scoring.
Batch long transcripts into overlapping windows of 30 with stride 10 and stitch boundaries via max voting (paper-2 Section 3.2).
Run eval-001 on the test set; P_k must be <= the paper-1 TeT+CLS baseline on the same corpus (40.49 on DialSeg_711, 54.34 on Doc2Dial -- paper-1 Table 4).
features.notes: Sử dụng AI model thứ nhất: NSP BERT từ paper-1. Paper-2 Section 3.2 trained hierarchical_segment as a BART classifier on 12,600 UHRS-annotated meetings; the project instead reuses the unsupervised TextTiling + NSP-BERT pipeline from paper-1 because it does not require crowd-labelled boundaries. The 30-utterance window / 10-utterance stride / 8-utt chunk size are derived from the 8-words-per-utterance heuristic (Banerjee et al.) and the 1 token = 0.75 words heuristic (paper-2 Section 3.3). The 6..10 segment-count tolerance on the committee sample is a smoke test, not a quality bar; the real bar is eval-001's P_k against paper-1's TeT+CLS baseline.

features.title: Implement Hierarchical Chunking (8-utterance blocks)
features.user_visible_behavior: Given a SegmentResult with more than 8 utterances, ChunkingService returns an ordered list of Chunks each containing <= 8 contiguous utterances, ready to be fed into the abstractive summarizer.
verification: Chunk a 50-utterance segment and assert exactly 7 chunks (6 of size 8 + 1 of size 2) with no chunk exceeding MAX_CHUNK_SIZE.
Reject attempts to materialize a chunk with > MAX_CHUNK_SIZE utterances (Pydantic validator at the types layer).
Preserve the original utterance ordering inside each chunk so that rolling summaries remain chronologically correct.
Return chunks whose utterances reference the parent SegmentResult.utterances_start + offset (no copies).

End-to-end on data/eval_vi/meeting_committee.json[0] (370 utts, 8 segments with lengths [13,32,33,16,27,130,118,1]) produces 50 chunks -- the same count reported by tests/manual/test_meeting_committee_sample.py and progress.md.
features.notes: Trực tiếp từ paper-2 Section 3.2: 8-utterance chunks are the input size for hierarchical_abstractive. The Chunk model already enforces MAX_CHUNK_SIZE=8 (model-001). Note that per-segment chunking yields 50 chunks (not ceil(370/8)=47) because each segment's remainder produces an extra short chunk; this is verified by the manual test.

features.title: Implement Hierarchical Summarization (deBERTa abstractive + title)
features.user_visible_behavior: For each SegmentResult the service generates a chapter title (hierarchical_title) and a 3rd-person abstractive rolling summary per 8-utterance Chunk (hierarchical_abstractive), then attaches both back to the SegmentResult.
verification: Generate a chapter title for a SegmentResult of >= 8 utterances and assert it is non-empty.
Generate a 3rd-person rolling summary for each Chunk and assert it preserves chronological order.
Confirm abstractive summaries for an empty chunk raise a typed ValidationError.
Confirm the 512-token surrounding context window from paper-2 Section 3.3 is enforced in the prompt/tokenizer call.
Confirm each generated title is written to SegmentResult.title and each chunk summary is written to Chunk.rolling_summary (not just returned).
features.notes: Paper-2 Section 3.2: hierarchical_abstractive is a fine-tuned deBERTa trained on 1M 8-utterance dialogue -> 3rd-person summary pairs. hierarchical_title is a deBERTa trained on 1M utterance -> topic pairs. Both run with 512-token context. Paper-2 does not specify a hard title-length cap, so verification asserts non-empty rather than a word count.

features.title: Implement Highlights Pipeline (extractive BART + abstractive deBERTa)
features.user_visible_behavior: Given a DialogueTranscript, HighlightsService returns a list of (text, type, source) triples: type KEY_POINT (UI: 'note') for general highlights, type ACTION_ITEM (UI: 'task') for action items. Text is rephrased in 3rd person using the abstractive deBERTa (paper-2 Section 3.2).
verification: Run the pipeline on a known committee transcript sample and recover at least one ACTION_ITEM whose text matches a manually identified task.
Run the pipeline and assert every returned highlight has HighlightType in {KEY_POINT, ACTION_ITEM} and HighlightSource.AUTO.
Assert each key point sits inside a 106-token (~10-utterance) context window (paper-2 Section 3.3).
Reject empty highlight text.
features.notes: Paper-2 Section 3.2: highlights_extractive (BART) selects the important utterances, highlights_abstractive (deBERTa) rephrases them in 3rd person within a 512-token context. The two-step decomposition (select -> rephrase) is preserved. Paper-2 does not specify a maximum summary length, so this feature intentionally does not assert one -- a future config-001 follow-up may add a tunable cap if needed.

features.title: Implement MeetingRecapOrchestrator (end-to-end pipeline)
features.user_visible_behavior: Given a TranscriptIngestionRequest, the orchestrator runs CoherenceScorer -> TextTiling -> Chunker -> hierarchical_summarizer -> highlights_pipeline and returns a complete HierarchicalRecap with non-empty segments, non-empty chunks, and (when applicable) non-empty highlights_notes and highlights_tasks.
verification: End-to-end run on data/eval_vi/meeting_committee.json[0] produces a HierarchicalRecap with segment_count == 8, total_chunks == 50, and len(highlights_notes) + len(highlights_tasks) >= 1 (matches tests/manual/test_meeting_committee_sample.py output).
Run on a 2-utterance transcript and assert a single SegmentResult of length 2 with 1 chunk is produced.
Run on an empty transcript and assert a typed ValidationError (not a generic 500).
Persist the meeting_id -> recap mapping via the file repository (model-002) for later retrieval.
Populate HierarchicalRecap.processing_time_ms with the wall-clock duration of the full pipeline.
features.notes: Wire-up: SegmenterService -> ChunkingService -> HierarchicalSummarizationService + HighlightsService. The orchestrator owns the meeting_id lifecycle and processing_time_ms metric, both of which are first-class fields on HierarchicalRecap. The manual test (tests/manual/test_meeting_committee_sample.py) already produces segment_count=8, total_chunks=50, 1 note, 1 task -- those are the exact numbers the orchestrator must match once the real services replace the placeholder chunk/segment construction.

Paper-2 Section 3.4 also says hierarchical chapter summaries cannot be deleted; the API must reject DELETE on /segments/{sid}/summary.

features.title: Hierarchical Tab UI (chapterized minutes with progressive disclosure)
features.user_visible_behavior: The 'Hierarchical' tab renders the meeting as a chronological list of chapter cards. Each card shows the auto-generated title, an inline-editable title field, a star count for key points, a checkbox count for tasks, and a collapsed view of 8-utterance chunk summaries that expand on click to reveal the raw transcript (paper-2 Section 3.4).
verification: Confirm chapter cards render in chronological order (utterances_start ascending).
Inline-edit a chapter title and confirm PUT /api/v1/meetings/{id}/segments/{sid} persists the change; reload and confirm the new title survives.

Confirm a chapter with >= 1 key point shows a star icon, a chapter with >= 1 action item shows a checkbox icon, and a chapter with neither shows no badge -- counts come from the segment-scoped highlights (filtered by Highlight.segment_id, or via a dedicated GET /api/v1/meetings/{id}/segments/{sid}/highlights endpoint).
Click a chunk card and confirm the 8-utterance raw transcript is revealed (progressive disclosure -- paper-2 Section 5.3.1 'progressive detail').
Confirm collapsing a chapter hides the chunk summaries but keeps the title visible.
Confirm chapter summaries cannot be deleted from the UI (paper-2 Section 3.4 -- 'summaries couldn't be deleted' in hierarchical view).
features.notes: Phần trình diễn sản phẩm cuối cùng. Paper-2 Section 5.3.1: participants use a progressive, breadth-first exploration strategy -- chapter heading first, then per-chunk summaries, then raw utterances. The 'collapse chapter' affordance (paper-2 Section 5.3.3) lets users tune their preferred depth. Per-chapter star/checkbox counts depend on a way to scope highlights to a segment; the simplest path is to filter HierarchicalRecap.all_highlights by segment_id, but a dedicated endpoint is cleaner.

Click 'Show context' on a key point; confirm the transcript view scrolls to the source chunk and reveals the 3 utterances before and 3 utterances after the source utterance (paper-2 Section 3.4).

features.title: Quantitative Segmentation Evaluation (P_k, Win-Diff, F1)
features.user_visible_behavior: Running the evaluation harness on the Vietnamese-translated test sets in data/eval_vi/ produces a paper-1-style table with P_k, Win-Diff, and F1 scores for our CoherenceScorer + TextTiling pipeline.
verification: Run `python -m src.evaluation.segmentation_eval --corpus dialseg_711` and confirm a P_k, Win-Diff, F1 row is printed per method.
Run the same command for --corpus doc2dial, meeting_ami, meeting_icsi, meeting_committee, tiage (all present in data/eval_vi/).
For ZYS (Chinese, paper-1 Table 5) the harness must accept --corpus zys and source ZYS from an external path (data/eval_vi/zys.json is not shipped -- see data-001 / `data_corpus_note`).

Compare against the paper-1 TeT+CLS baseline (P_k 40.49 on DialSeg_711, 54.34 on Doc2Dial -- paper-1 Table 4). The Vietnamese-translated test sets are not directly comparable to paper-1's English numbers, so the eval must report absolute numbers and flag the language mismatch.
Confirm depth-score variance (paper-1 Table 6) is computed and reported per corpus.
features.notes: Paper-1 Section 4.3: metrics are P_k (Beeferman et al., 1999), Win-Diff (Pevzner and Hearst, 2002), and F1. Lower P_k/WD is better, higher F1 is better. Window size k should match the median ground-truth segment length per corpus. The test sets in data/eval_vi/ are Vietnamese translations, so direct numerical comparison with paper-1 Table 4 is not valid; eval-001 should still produce the table for internal tracking, but the comparison-vs-baseline bar must be reframed as 'does Vietnamese NSP-BERT perform comparably to Vietnamese TeT+CLS' rather than 'does it match paper-1's English numbers'.

features.title: Qualitative Recap Evaluation Harness (user-study script)
features.user_visible_behavior: An evaluator script can run a small-N user study (target N=7 like paper-2 Section 4) that captures per-participant behavior for each of the 13 meeting-habit constructs in paper-2 Table 4 and the 9 finding rows in paper-2 Table 5.
verification: Run `python -m src.evaluation.user_study --participant P01 --meeting data/eval_vi/meeting_committee.json` and confirm a per-participant JSON report is written.
Confirm the script records add/edit/delete/star/check events on highlights and chapter-title edits, with timestamps.
Confirm it captures per-participant answers to: 'useful for personal work?', 'useful for group work?', 'edit confidence for highlights vs hierarchical' (paper-2 Section 5.2-5.3).
Confirm the consolidated report includes the Table-4 habit counts and the Table-5 finding matrix.
Confirm the harness can be replayed against stored event logs (no need to re-run the live UI) so the study is reproducible from repo artifacts only.
features.notes: Paper-2 Section 4: 7 participants at Microsoft, pre-recorded real meetings. Paper-2 Table 4: 13 meeting-habit constructs (Takes notes ... Recap at end of meeting). Paper-2 Table 5: 9 finding rows comparing highlights vs hierarchical recaps. The harness should be reproducible from repo artifacts only -- no out-of-band chat context. The original study was conducted in English; running it on Vietnamese data (data/eval_vi/meeting_committee.json) requires translated instruments.
